# Commands

Inspect the window with `herdr-app ls` and `herdr-app status`.
`herdr-app commands` lists the app actions below, even without an open window.

Run an action in the open window with `herdr-app do`:

```sh
herdr-app do pane.split --direction right
herdr-app do pane.split '{"direction":"right"}'
```

Arguments can be named flags or one JSON object. Required arguments are marked below.
Actions use the current selection unless you give an explicit target.
Some actions close terminals; read their descriptions before running them.
Mods can add their own actions, which are not listed here.

## `space.new`

Make a space: its name (default: none, so it's called after where its first terminal is), the folder its terminals start in (default: the focused terminal's), its first tab's name (default: none, so it's called by its number), optionally an agent (argv) and its first message (task), and the machine it lives on (`hc machine ls`; default the focused space's machine for keys and clicks, this computer for scripts; empty string: this computer; its terminals start in that machine's home unless folder).

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `name` | no |
| `folder` | no |
| `tab` | no |
| `argv` | no |
| `task` | no |
| `machine` | no |

## `space.close`

Close a space and end its terminals (asks first unless confirmed).

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `id` | no |
| `confirmed` | no |

## `space.rename`

Rename a space (asks the person when no name; an empty name: called after where its first terminal is again).

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `id` | no |
| `name` | no |

## `space.move`

Move a space to a position (1 = first).

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `id` | yes |
| `index` | yes |

## `tab.new`

Make a tab in a space (default: the selected one; name default: none, so it's called by its number) with a terminal in folder (default: the focused terminal's), optionally an agent (argv) and its first message (task); or with a mod as its only pane (`mod`, its `props`: a file, a board). With no space open, a person's new tab starts a space (as space.new).

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `name` | no |
| `space` | no |
| `folder` | no |
| `argv` | no |
| `task` | no |
| `mod` | no |
| `props` | no |

## `tab.close`

Close a tab and end its terminals.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `id` | no |
| `confirmed` | no |

## `tab.rename`

Rename a tab (asks the person when no name; an empty name: called by its number again).

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `id` | no |
| `name` | no |

## `tab.move`

Move a tab to a position in its space (1 = first).

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `id` | yes |
| `index` | yes |

## `pane.split`

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `direction` | yes |
| `pane` | no |
| `argv` | no |
| `mod` | no |
| `props` | no |

## `pane.close`

Close a pane and end its terminal.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `pane` | no |

## `pane.rename`

Name a pane (default: the focused one; asks the person when no name, starting from the name it shows: its own or, with pane_auto_names, its automatic one; an empty name: its program's again).

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `pane` | no |
| `name` | no |

## `terminal.open`

Start a terminal: as a new tab (place "tab", default), or "right"/"down" of the focused pane.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `argv` | no |
| `folder` | no |
| `place` | no |
| `name` | no |

## `terminal.popup`

Run a program on this computer in a popup over the tab (terminal.peek's, with keep-as-tab and close), started without a parent. It closes when the program ends, and the terminal goes with it unless wait is true, which keeps it until `{"wait": terminal}` on the control socket (as `herdr-app popup` sends) has read its exit code and signal (unread for a minute, it goes too). cwd: where it starts (default: home); hold: keep it up after the program ends until a key (not on Windows); width, height: the popup's size (px, or a fraction of the window up to 1; default 0.8). ✕ hides the popup and the program keeps running until the next popup, which ends the program the last popup started, open or hidden.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `argv` | yes |
| `cwd` | no |
| `hold` | no |
| `wait` | no |
| `width` | no |
| `height` | no |

## `terminal.keep`

Give a running terminal without a pane (a sub-agent) a pane: a new tab, or "right"/"down".

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `terminal` | yes |
| `place` | no |

## `terminal.park`

Take a terminal's pane away and disable core keep; it keeps running (a sub-agent shows under its parent again).

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `terminal` | yes |

## `terminal.right_click`

Where right-clicks in a terminal (default: the focused one) go when its program takes the mouse: "program" or "menu" (Herdr's, the default). Shift+right-click is always the menu.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `to` | yes |
| `terminal` | no |

## `terminal.pin`

Pin an agent to the top of the agent lists (pinned true) or unpin it (false). Pins are kept with the terminal, so every Herdr client shows them, and end with it.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `terminal` | yes |
| `pinned` | yes |

## `terminal.kill`

End a terminal and its sub-agents.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `terminal` | yes |

## `session.resume`

Resume the recorded agents (programs with a `resume` rule in programs.json, such as Claude Code) whose terminals are back to a bare shell, typically after a restart: types `cd <folder> && <command>` into each (default: every one; terminal: just that one). Asks first unless confirmed; scripts pass confirmed: true. Skips, and says why, a terminal not running, running something else, or sharing its session with another.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `terminal` | no |
| `confirmed` | no |

## `session.saved`

List the recorded agents session.resume would bring back, each with its terminal, where, folder, command line and session, and whether it can be resumed now (ready, else why not).

No arguments.

## `pane.zoom_text_in`

Make a terminal pane's text bigger (default: the focused terminal) by one zoom step, on top of the app's zoom; its program gets the new rows and columns. Kept for the life of the pane's terminal view.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `pane` | no |

## `pane.zoom_text_out`

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `pane` | no |

## `pane.zoom_text_reset`

Put a terminal pane's text (default: the focused terminal) back at the app's size.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|

## `pane.focus`

Focus a pane (or the pane showing a terminal).

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `pane` | no |
| `terminal` | no |

## `pane.go`

Focus the pane or focusable mod to the "left", "right", "up" or "down".

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `direction` | yes |

## `pane.swap`

Swap the focused pane with its neighbor in a direction.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `direction` | yes |

## `pane.arrange`

Rearrange a tab's panes (default: the shown tab) evenly: "tiled" (a grid), "bsp" (each pane takes half of what's left, right then down), "master" (the focused pane on the left half, the rest stacked on the right), "columns", "rows", "next" (the mode after the tab's last one, from tiled), or "off". Panes keep their terminals and go in reading order (top to bottom, then left to right); a zoomed pane unzooms. The tab keeps its mode: a pane split into it or closed in it arranges it again, a new pane right after the one it split. In "bsp" the tree stays instead, as in tuios and bspwm: a split halves the pane it splits in the direction asked, and a closed pane's space goes back to the pane it was split with. "off" clears the mode and leaves the panes where they are.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `mode` | yes |
| `tab` | no |

## `focus.toggle_follows_mouse`

Turn focus follows mouse on or off (settings.json's focus_follows_mouse): the pointer resting on a terminal pane focuses it.

No arguments.

## `terminal.peek`

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|

## `terminal.show`

Show a terminal in a pane for now, in place of its own (no terminal: back).

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `terminal` | no |
| `pane` | no |

## `terminal.copy`

Copy the focused terminal's selection. With nothing selected, that key goes to the program.

No arguments.

## `terminal.scroll`

Scroll a terminal's view of its history (default: the focused one). Give exactly one of: lines (a whole number; negative goes up, toward history), pages (a number, fractions allowed; one page is the terminal's rows), to: "top" (oldest history) or "bottom" (the live screen). This scrolls Herdr's view, not the program.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `lines` | no |
| `pages` | no |
| `to` | no |
| `terminal` | no |

## `terminal.paste`

Paste into the focused terminal (copied files as if dropped; an image alone as terminal.paste_image pastes it).

No arguments.

## `terminal.paste_image`

Ctrl+V: the clipboard's image as a file on the focused terminal's machine, when that's another one; on Windows, paste clipboard text; otherwise Ctrl+V goes to the terminal.

No arguments.

## `terminal.search`

Search the focused terminal's screen and scrollback; the find bar and query stay with that terminal.

No arguments.

## `layout.spacing`

Space around the shown tab's panes, px 0 to 40, kept with the layout's clicks (its file is not changed; a later edit of the same field in the file wins): pane_gap (between panes: the tab block's pane.gap), area_padding (number or [y, x]) and area_gap (the row or column holding the tab block), terminal_padding ([x, y]: the layout root's). reset: a list of those names, back to the file's values.

| Argument | Required |
|---|---|
| `pane_gap` | no |
| `area_padding` | no |
| `area_gap` | no |
| `terminal_padding` | no |
| `reset` | no |

## `layout.reset`

|---|---|
